blogs.title: When ‘Deconditioning’ Isn’t: Progressive Proximal Weakness After GLP-1 Agonist Exposure
blogs.description: This post would explore the diagnostic pivot from presumed post-hospital deconditioning to inflammatory myopathy in a patient with worsening proximal weakness, dysphagia, and dysphonia after semaglutide exposure. It would highlight red flags that should trigger reconsideration of the diagnosis, including rising CK, bulbar symptoms, and loss of independent sitting or standing, and discuss how clinicians can avoid anchoring on a benign recovery narrative after an initial medication intolerance admission.

blogs.title: Rhabdo or IMNM? Sorting Out CK Elevation After a New Metabolic Drug
blogs.description: This post would focus on the key clinical distinctions between acute toxic rhabdomyolysis and immune-mediated necrotising myopathy. Using this case, it would compare tempo of illness, magnitude and trajectory of CK elevation, expected response to drug withdrawal alone, biopsy findings, and need for immunosuppression. It would also place the case in the context of prior reports of GLP-1-related muscle injury and explain why a delayed, progressive course argues for an autoimmune process rather than direct muscle toxicity.

blogs.title: Seronegative Necrotising Myopathy: What to Do When HMGCR and SRP Are Negative
blogs.description: This post would review the practical work-up of suspected IMNM in a patient with negative myositis serologies. It would discuss the limitations of antibody panels, the importance of MRI and muscle biopsy, and how pathology showing myofiber necrosis, myophagocytosis, macrophage-predominant inflammation, and membrane attack complex deposition can establish the diagnosis despite negative HMGCR and SRP antibodies. The post would also address how seronegativity complicates causal inference and broadens the search for novel triggers.

blogs.title: Dysphagia, Dysphonia, and Weakness: Treating Severe IMNM Before the Window Closes
blogs.description: This post would examine early management decisions in severe suspected inflammatory myopathy, especially when bulbar involvement is present. It would cover the rationale for pulse-dose methylprednisolone followed by high-dose prednisone and IVIG, when to escalate treatment before all confirmatory data are back, and how short-course therapy may be sufficient in drug-triggered disease compared with idiopathic IMNM. The discussion would emphasize balancing urgency of treatment against diagnostic uncertainty.

blogs.title: AST, ALT, and CK: Don’t Let ‘Liver Disease’ Hide a Myopathy
blogs.description: This post would use the patient’s longstanding steatotic liver disease and transaminase elevation to discuss a common diagnostic trap: assuming AST/ALT abnormalities are purely hepatic in origin. It would review how muscle injury contributes to transaminase elevation, how to interpret liver enzymes in the setting of CK elevation, and how coexisting NAFLD can obscure recognition of myositis. The post would provide a practical framework for separating hepatic from muscular sources of abnormal aminotransferases.

blogs.title: The Semaglutide Era and Rare Harm Signals: How Clinicians Should Think About Pharmacovigilance
blogs.description: This post would address the broader implications of a probable semaglutide-associated IMNM in the context of rapidly expanding GLP-1 receptor agonist use. It would discuss causality assessment in single-case reports, why rechallenge is often neither feasible nor ethical, and how bedside clinicians should report unusual immune-mediated toxicities. The article would also consider whether some adverse muscle events attributed to weight-loss drugs may represent underrecognized autoimmune syndromes rather than expected sarcopenia or medication intolerance.
